title: Clean design and practical patterns — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: An order service chooses a pricing policy without a growing conditional. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Only when no validation is needed
Readable construction with many optional settings

questions.explanation: A builder can organize construction choices and validate them.

questions.prompt: What should be in place before refactoring a pricing rule?

options.text: A second implementation of every getter

questions.explanation: Behavior tests detect accidental changes during restructuring.

questions.prompt: Does List.copyOf deeply freeze mutable element objects?

options.text: Only for lists of size one

questions.explanation: It copies the collection structure, not the internals of each element.

questions.prompt: What does dependency inversion encourage at a variable boundary?

options.text: Instantiate every vendor class inside every method
Use static state for all collaborators

questions.explanation: A focused contract lets higher-level policy avoid vendor details.

questions.prompt: When should a factory add value?

options.text: Only when no objects are created
To hide every simple record constructor
When it centralizes meaningful construction decisions

questions.explanation: A factory earns its place through construction policy.

questions.prompt: What is a warning sign of unnecessary abstraction?

options.text: A simple rule becomes harder to follow without a change benefit
A focused interface at an external boundary

questions.explanation: Abstractions should make the relevant changes easier.
